newsitem.title: UK: Carlton snatches Westcountry tv in surprise move.
newsitem.headline: Carlton snatches Westcountry tv in surprise move.

text.p: Britain's Carlton Communications said on Saturday it had acquired the small Westcountry television station in a surprise move that established Carlton as the country's biggest commercial television broadcaster.
Carlton, which already owns the independent licence for weekday television in the London region and the English Midlands, clinched the 85 million sterling ($142.8 million) deal in an agreed bid.
But Carlton's move astounded the commercial television industry which had been expecting rival media group United News and Media to announce its own takeover early next week.
Media industry sources said last week that United had all but completed agreement with Westcountry but was trying to negotiate the price down to a reported 65 million sterling.
"It is a pretty audacious move," one highly-placed industry source told Reuters on Saturday. "The sum of 85 million is big money."
Westcountry, a private company with 1995 profits of five million sterling, holds the licence for much of southwestern England.
The deal gives Carlton a broadcast audience of 22 million people or 38 percent of the population, making it the largest commercial television operator in Britain.

"Westcountry is a successful ITV company and we will build on its strengths. With Carlton, Central and Westcountry we will continue to enhance ITV's reputation as Britain's most popular channel," said Carlton chairman Michael Green.

United News operates commercial television (ITV) licences in southern England through its Meridian unit and eastern England where it runs Anglia TV. Last month it took a 20 percent stake in HTV, the ITV company for Wales and west England.
The acquisition of Westcountry would have strengthened its domination of Wales and a large slice of southern and western England.
"Michael Green's audacious move has blasted that (plan) to bits," said an industry source. "It is a corporate move...he doesn't want United to control the south of England."
A United spokesman said it had been evident for some days that Westcountry was having discussions with another party.
"We put forward our best offer and Carlton offered substantially more. We have no regrets," a United spokesman told Reuters. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds Sterling)
